item.title: Re: Effect of laughter exercise versus 0.1% sodium hyaluronic acid on ocular surface discomfort in dry eye disease: non-inferiority randomised controlled trial
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, I read with interest the randomised non-inferiority trial evaluating laughter exercise as an intervention for dry eye disease. The authors should be commended for exploring a creative, low-cost, and patient-centred approach to a condition that is both common and often frustrating for patients and clinicians alike. item.title: Beyond exit headlines: Taiwan’s lesson on health resilience in an era of fragmentation
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Looi’s report on the United States’ contested departure from the World Health Organization (WHO) illustrates more than a legal dispute—it signals a broader shift toward fragmented health governance. item.title: FDA bayesian clinical trials may speed approvals only if priors are made clinically legible, with stronger disclosure of uncertainty, not more sophisticated opacity
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Doshi’s report on the FDA’s draft guidance (1) encouraging Bayesian methodology for primary inference in pivotal drug and biologic trials captures a real opportunity and a real hazard at the same time. item.title: Rethinking reliance on intraocular pressure in glaucoma detection
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, The EPIC-Norfolk Eye Study provides valuable population-based data on glaucoma prevalence in the UK and reinforces an important clinical message: reliance on intraocular pressure (IOP) alone is an unreliable way to detect glaucoma. item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, This engaging analysis usefully quantifies a familiar experience for many clinicians: the tendency for the word “recent” in academic writing to stretch well beyond what most readers would intuitively consider recent. item.title: Re: HPV: Vaccine uptake far below pre-pandemic level as 1 in 4 children leave school unprotected
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, I am suprised that these data are presented without mention of the uptake required for "herd" or "population immunity" being mentioned. item.title: Race is not that competitive anymore
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor From time immemorial, the idea of race has been a source of pride and prejudice—fueling divisions between neighbours, battles between friends, and wars between nations, often with immense human suffering and bloodshed. item.title: Re: Experiences of access to general practice in England: qualitative study and implications for the NHS 10 year plan
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Sinnott and colleagues’ qualitative study provides a timely and important corrective to the prevailing assumption that problems of access in general practice are primarily technical and can be resolved through digitisation, service reconfiguration, or task substitution alone.
